details:
PULSE — Astronaut Health Monitoring

Overview

PULSE is a mobile health monitoring application prototype designed to help astronauts track and understand their physical condition during long-duration space missions.

Spaceflight exposes the human body to unique challenges, including microgravity, radiation, isolation, and physiological stress. Monitoring health indicators is therefore essential, especially when immediate medical assistance from Earth may not be available.

Our goal is to make health monitoring more accessible, understandable, and convenient for astronauts.

How PULSE Works

PULSE organizes health measurements into four main categories:

  • Blood: Blood-related health indicators.
  • Urine: Urinary health indicators.
  • Non-invasive: Measurements that do not require invasive procedures.
  • Eye Health: Indicators related to vision and ocular health.

The application provides a dashboard that summarizes available health information and allows users to navigate between different categories and individual indicators.

Astronauts can manually enter new measurements, save them, and review previous results. Each indicator has a dedicated screen displaying its measurement history and a chart showing changes over time.

PULSE also uses color-coded statuses to distinguish measurements within reference ranges from values that may require attention. When a measurement falls outside its reference range, the application displays a warning and contextual recommendations.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main benefit of PULSE is bringing multiple categories of health information into one accessible interface.

By combining measurement records, visual trends, status indicators, and recommendations, PULSE aims to reduce the effort required to review health information and help astronauts recognize potentially important changes.

The project is intended to support greater awareness of personal health during space missions and provide a foundation for more advanced astronaut health monitoring systems.

Technologies Used

PULSE was developed using:

  • Flutter and Dart for cross-platform mobile application development.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration.
  • Visual Studio Code as a development environment.
  • Flutter charting libraries for visualizing measurement history.

The prototype was developed and tested using an Android development environment.

Creativity and Design

Our approach focuses on making complex health information easier to understand through a minimalistic, dark-themed interface.

Instead of presenting measurements only as numbers, PULSE combines visual charts, color-coded health statuses, historical records, and contextual recommendations.

We designed the interface to help users quickly identify relevant information and navigate between medical indicators without unnecessary complexity.

Development Considerations and Future Work

During development, we considered usability, readability, data visualization, and the potential difficulties of monitoring health during long-duration space missions.

The current prototype demonstrates manual measurement entry, visualization of measurement history, and status-based feedback.

Future development could include automated data collection from compatible medical sensors, personalized health monitoring, secure data exchange with medical professionals, and further validation of health indicators against space medicine requirements.

PULSE is a functional prototype, not a clinically validated medical diagnostic system. Its purpose is to demonstrate how digital tools could make astronaut health monitoring more efficient and accessible.


Source code you can find on GitHub: https://github.com/cherenov/PULSE
